text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Truck drivers harden protest, block towns, petrol depots and harbours. Government is expected to make a gesture.
-- Industry chiefs worried about rate of 990 lira to a mark chosen for the lira's re-entry into the European monetary system.
-- Eurotunnel shares tumble in London and Paris as doubt rises on length and cost of repairs following last week's fire.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Railway operators consider legal action against Eurotunnel for losses linked to failure to open tunnel facilities.
-- Saint-Gobain considers selling water supply subsidiary Cise to Bouygues.
-- Thomson's defence unit Thomson-CSF considers cutting up to 5,000 jobs through 1997, following drop in demand linked to defence sector restructuring.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin may announce today that pre-1917 Russian bonds could be reimbursed.
-- 30 percent of the world's active population is unemployed, according to International Labour Organisation.
L'AGEFI
-- Insurer AGF shares could go up by 20 percent, according to a study by BNP Equities.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Alcatel chairman Serge Tchuruk allegedly prepares new bid for Thomson to be presented if sale to Lagardere Groupe is not effective by December 31.
-- Member of Bank of France monetary policy council Paul Marchelli says franc is 10 percent overvalued against the dollar due to the mark-franc parity, calls for rate cuts to jump start the economy.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Eurotunnel faces demand for compensation from French, British and Belgian train operators.
